summary: This Makefile provides a command-line interface for building and running a Docker-based blog project in either development or production mode. It defines helper targets that wrap Docker and Docker Compose commands, automatically extracting the current user's ID and group ID to pass into containers, and provides colored output to make console messages more readable. The user can switch between development and production environments by setting the TARGET variable.

explanations.3: SHELL:=bash tells Make to use bash instead of the default shell (sh), which gives access to bash-specific features like arrays and extended syntax.
explanations.8: $(shell id -u) runs the id command and captures its output, storing the current user's numeric ID so containers can run with matching permissions.
explanations.9: $(shell id -g) does the same thing but gets the group ID instead, ensuring files created in containers have the right ownership.
explanations.13: TARGET ?= development sets TARGET to 'development' only if it hasn't been set already on the command line or in the environment, allowing overrides.
explanations.21: This defines a color code template using ANSI escape sequences that printf will use to print colored text; \033 is the escape character.
explanations.29: .PHONY tells Make that 'help' is not a real file to build, just a command to run.
explanations.32: The awk command parses this Makefile itself to extract lines with ## comments and formats them into a help menu automatically.
explanations.38: bash: _bash-$(TARGET) means the 'bash' target depends on either '_bash-development' or '_bash-production' depending on what TARGET is set to.
explanations.46: @printf $(_YELLOW) prints using the yellow color template defined earlier; the @ suppresses Make from echoing the command itself.
explanations.47: DOCKER_UID=${DOCKER_UID} DOCKER_GID=${DOCKER_GID} passes the captured user and group IDs as environment variables into the docker compose command.
explanations.59: @for dir in .docusaurus node_modules; do starts a bash loop that runs inside Make; the @-prefix hides the loop commands from output.
explanations.60: [ ! -d "$$dir" ] checks if the directory doesn't exist; the $$ is doubled because Make interprets single $ as its own variable syntax.
explanations.67: _build-development: _ensure-host-volumes means this target first runs the _ensure-host-volumes target to create folders before building.
explanations.71: ${ARGS} allows the user to pass extra flags through the make command like 'make build ARGS="--no-cache"'.
explanations.92: docker run --rm cleans up the container when it exits; the --user root flag runs the command with root privileges inside the container.
explanations.97: @docker stop blog > /dev/null 2>&1 || true stops the container, redirects all output to /dev/null to hide it, and the || true ensures Make continues even if the container doesn't exist.
explanations.127: @-docker stops on failure (-prefix) and suppresses output (@ prefix); the || true makes the command always succeed so the next line runs.
explanations.129: -d runs the container in the background (detached mode), --publish maps port 443 on the host to 443 in the container, and --name gives the container a label.
